title: AI is great
direction: Illustrative one-shot montage. Game, landing page, app.
check: Use motion graphics for the opening example. No stopwatch or performance claim.
lines: AI is great.

title: At first
direction: Hold on the app. Drop music, then show contradictory specs, one cross-cutting rule and refactoring risk.
check: The same working screen carries through S01–S02. This is an illustration.
lines: At first.
And then you try to scale.
Who decided that, and why?
The specs disagree. One little change touches half the app. Suddenly, cleaning it up feels risky.
What if we could build software differently?

title: Name authoring
direction: 00:38 bring Request into the center. At 00:43 branch it into Intention, Requirements, Decisions and Reasons. At 00:51 bring in the Authoring title and hold.
check: Build the four labels as editable vector titles.
lines: What if, instead of just generating code, we could capture what you actually mean?
Your intentions. Your requirements. Your decisions. And the reasons behind them.
That's what we're building.
We call it authoring.

title: Request into interpretation
direction: 00:54 open the approved disposable authoring fixture at the request field. Enter “Track equipment loans so staff can see what is out.” At 01:01 show the recorded request beside the actual interpretation and its visible assumption or open decision.
check: Capture the request and the resulting interpretation in one continuous take. A basic intent form alone cannot prove semantic decomposition. Use a marked temp card if the proof is unavailable.
lines: You describe what you want to create.
Sorcery decomposes your request into meaningful, reusable building blocks.
It shows you what it understands, what it's assuming, and where important decisions need to be made.

title: Preview an alternative
direction: 01:10 select the other supported choice from the same saved request. Hold the changed consequence and the available review action for the final three seconds.
check: Two replayable choices and a consequence before commitment are required. If the interaction stops at a proposal, label the slot as missing in the review cut.
lines: You can explore alternatives, change your mind, and see the consequences before committing.

title: Rules and reasons
direction: 01:19 introduce Temple. At 01:25 connect a Record, a Rule and a Decision as a simple diagram. At 01:33 cut to the matching rule or receipt in the actual capture.
check: Illustration explains the relationship. The actual receipt supports whatever provenance can be read on screen.
lines: Underneath it all is Temple.
A new kind of relational database and execution engine, where your software, its meaning, and the rules that govern it live together.
Everything is connected.
Every important decision can have a reason.
Every change can have provenance.
And every action can be subject to explicit constraints.
We call these admissibility gates.

title: The gate decides
direction: 01:42 frame the guarded command and its condition. At 01:47 show the refusal with the condition unsatisfied. At 01:52 repeat the same action after satisfying that condition and hold the outcome.
check: Use the supported Encounter guarded-command fixture. Keep the command and other inputs fixed, and record the changed condition explicitly.
lines: Instead of giving AI unrestricted access and hoping it behaves, Temple is designed to enforce what it's allowed to do.
Your AI works within your rules.
Not the other way around.

title: Compose through a seam
direction: 01:57 show two capability blocks. At 02:02 reveal the mismatched field meanings. At 02:06 connect them through a labelled mapping and hold the translated value.
check: Use the actual fields and mapping once qualified. A diagram with a TEMP label can occupy this slot in the internal cut.
lines: And here's where things get interesting.
Your software doesn't have to be perfect on day one.
Start simple.
Reuse existing capabilities.
Connect systems that don't quite agree using explicit seams.
Improve the parts that matter.

title: Change the implementation
direction: 02:10 place Before and After side by side. At 02:17 highlight the changed implementation step. At 02:24 reveal the same named behavior check and both outcomes.
check: Capture two real revisions and one replayable check. A visual resemblance does not qualify the proof.
lines: As your requirements grow, you can decompose your application further, strengthen its assurances, and optimise its implementation.
Without unnecessarily changing its meaning.
Because you should be able to optimise how software works without changing what it's supposed to do.

title: Find the relevant context
direction: 02:31 frame the Context Hub query and run “Casimir boundary response” against the documented retrieval fixture. At 02:40 hold the ranked list. At 02:46 open the selected source and highlight its displayed link or inclusion reason.
check: Use a verified Observatory or equivalent capture with ranked output and trace. Clear visible credentials and unrelated research. This shows retrieval rather than an application-specific integration.
lines: Temple also makes your software navigable.
With Context Hub, graph-ranking techniques inspired by Google's PageRank help identify the information most relevant to a question.
So your AI can work with meaningful, connected context rather than trying to understand an entire codebase at once.

title: Choose an agent and model
direction: 02:53 reveal the agent and model as separate inputs to one workflow. At 02:58 use a real model choice or run label if qualified. End on the shared rules boundary.
check: The workbench Ollama run can show one local model. Broader bring-your-own support needs its own demonstrated or approved wording.
lines: Bring your own agent.
Choose your own models.
And keep the context where it belongs.

title: Who operates it
direction: 03:03 show one Temple system. At 03:08 split the operating arrangements into Self-hosted and Managed, with operator and data custody called out. At 03:16 return to one rules boundary.
check: Check the exact open-source scope and current managed offering before using those words in a release cut.
lines: Temple is built for sovereignty.
Open source.
Run it yourself, on your own infrastructure, with your own data.
Or use a managed platform if you'd rather leave the operations to us.
Your systems. Your rules. Your choice.

title: Recover the reason
direction: 03:21 return to the same behavior shown in the opening. At 03:27 reveal the saved reason from the authoring material, then at 03:32 show the corresponding rule or result if the two captures are linked.
check: Continuity check the opening and close. If proof sources differ, mark the linking graphic as illustrative.
lines: We believe the future of software isn't just about generating more code, faster.
It's about creating systems we can understand.
Systems we can trust.
Systems that preserve our intentions, adapt as our needs change, and remain under human control.

title: End card
direction: 03:38 reveal the three closing lines in order. At 03:47 resolve to the approved Sorcery and Temple wordmarks. Hold the final lockup to 03:52.
check: Confirm spelling, marks, and whether a call to action belongs on the end card. Keep the script’s closing words as the baseline.
lines: Software that remembers why.
Software that evolves without losing its meaning.
Software you author, not just program.
Welcome to Sorcery and Temple.
